| **Objective**       | This guideline helps developers choose the correct field sharing type when creating Sitecore template fields.<br><br>Use Versioned by default. Use Unversioned or Shared only when there is a clear requirement.<br><br>The sharing type affects how content behaves across languages and versions. Choosing the wrong type can cause unexpected content, workflow, or publishing behavior. |

## 1\. Typical real-world case: Site Schema Information

A common mistake is setting a field as **Shared** because the value looks like it should be the same across sites.

Template item path: /sitecore/templates/Feature/Brother Commerce/Commerce Schema Markup/Site Schema Information

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Actual Data: The same Site Schema Information has different values between EN and HK:

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## 2. Field Sharing Types

| **Type**    | **Language** | **Version** | **Typical Usage**                                         |
| ----------- | ------------ | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Versioned   | Different    | Different   | Normal content fields                                     |
| Unversioned | Different    | Same        | Language-specific content that does not change by version |
| Shared      | Same         | Same        | Truly global/technical values                             |

## 3. Versioned - Default

A Versioned field can have a different value for each language and version.

### Example

EN / Version 1 → "Brother Printer"

EN / Version 2 → "Brother Business Printer"

HK / Version 1 → "Brother Printer"

HK / Version 2 → "Brother Business Printer"

EN and HK can have different content, and each version can also have its own value.

### Use for

- Page Title
- Heading
- Description
- Rich Text
- Image
- CTA
- Link
- SEO content

Versioned should be the default for most content fields.

## 4. Unversioned

An Unversioned field can have a different value for each language, but the value is the same across all versions of that language.

### ****Example****

EN / Version 1 → "Printer"

EN / Version 2 → "Printer"

HK / Version 1 → "打印機"

HK / Version 2 → "打印機"

The EN value can be different from HK, but changing the value in one version also affects the other versions of the same language.

### Use only when

- The value needs to be different by language

## 5. Shared

A Shared field has one value across all languages and versions.

### Example

EN / Version 1 → Product Code = ABC123

EN / Version 2 → Product Code = ABC123

HK / Version 1 → Product Code = ABC123

HK / Version 2 → Product Code = ABC123

If the Product Code is changed, the new value applies to EN and HK and all versions.

### ****Typical use cases****

- External System ID
- Product Code
- Integration Identifier
- Technical/System Configuration

Shared should be treated as an exception, not the default.

## 6. Quick Decision Guide

Ask these questions before creating a field:

Does the value vary by language?

│

├── YES

│ │

│ └── Does the value vary by version?

│ ├── YES → VERSIONED

│ └── NO → UNVERSIONED

│

└── NO

│

└── Must exactly one value be used

across ALL languages and versions?

├── YES → SHARED

└── NO → Reconsider the field design
